messages:
sam: quick heads-up — seeing a spike of schema-rejects for fncall/tool responses that include extra top-level keys (e.g. "debug_info"). They get routed to degen and blow past the degen quota. dashboard: https://console/redwood/org/123/alerts
kevin: where are the responses coming from? new adapter/version? any sample payload?
sam: pasted a sanitized example below:
```json
{
  "result": {"text": "ok"},
  "debug_info": {"latency_ms": 23, "model_trace": []}
}
```
anya: hmm — why are we rejecting instead of coercing or dropping unknown fields? i thought soft-validate was on in the canary.
marta: this is also a UX problem: console only shows "schema reject" — we don't display the specific rule (extra_fields) or which route (degen) and users can't see quota impact at glance :thinking_face:
ops-bot: ALERT org-123 degen-route quota exceeded at 1734567905 — auto-throttle applied
kevin: two short options: (A) adapter whitelist unknown keys per-tool, or (B) enable soft_validate for the affected adapters and ship canary. Whitelist is more surgical but slower. I can PR the whitelist change.
sam: prefer soft_validate canary first so we can gather telemetry. proposal: add telemetry tag `validation.mode` (strict|soft|whitelist) and a `reject.reason` label with values like extra_fields/missing_required/type_mismatch. sample payloads should be stored for 48h. if reject-rate > 5% over 24h -> escalate to whitelist.
anya: i'll expose a console toggle for soft_validate per-route + a link to sampled payloads. also will add a "reason" column in the schema-reject dashboard and a chart for degen-route charge.
marta: owners: kevin -> adapter whitelist PR (if needed), anya -> console flag + dashboard columns, sam -> telemetry tagging + sampling retention. i'll open a tracking ticket and add canary rollout checklist.
sam: thanks — i'll kick off the metric collection and toggle soft_validate for a 5% traffic slice. :thumbsup:
